extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys and agents), USPTO OED staff, and others interested in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing professional conduct before the USPTO, examples of misconduct (failure to notify client), and the sanctions and administrative actions available/used by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects upon a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regulation provides a basis for disciplinary action where a practitioner's actions (including those described in other subsections) are deemed to adversely reflect on fitness to practice before the USPTO. In this case the respondent acknowledged violation of § 10.23(b)(6) via conduct in violation of § 10.23(c)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8) — duty to notify client of Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to inform a client of correspondence received from the Office when the correspondence (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) is received by the practitioner on behalf of a client or former client, and (iii) is correspondence of which a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client or former client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete application: Respondent received a Notice of Abandonment dated October 28, 2010 (for failure to timely reply to a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers) and did not notify the client; this conduct was the factual basis for the violation. Practitioners should notify clients promptly of Office correspondence that meets the three-part test in (i)-(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely response to Office notices (e.g., Notice to File Corrected Application Papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely reply to Office notices such as a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers can lead to a Notice of Abandonment for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners are expected to monitor and act on Office correspondence to avoid adverse outcomes (abandonment). Even if a practitioner fails to respond, the practitioner also has the duty to notify the client of such correspondence per § 10.23(c)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction of public reprimand and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose a public reprimand and require publication of the disciplinary order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the agreed sanction included: (a) a public reprimand; (b) publication of the Final Order in the OED Reading Room; and (c) publication of a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette. Publication of disciplinary decisions is part of the sanction/remedial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior discipline and use of record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of a disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing further complaints or in future disciplinary proceedings concerning the same respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This record can be used (1) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline for later misconduct, and/or (2) to rebut statements or representations by or on behalf of the respondent. The Final Order explicitly reserves the Office's right to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and procedural bases for settlement and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction and authority to approve settlement agreements and impose discipline pursuant to statutory and regulatory provisions such as 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26, and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements resolving disciplinary action are submitted for approval to the USPTO Director under the cited authorities; the Final Order and its publication follow the regulatory procedures referenced. The Agreement also specified allocation of costs (each party bears its own costs) as part of the settlement terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access to disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (electronic) and may be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order identifies URLs and indicates that the OED Reading Room is the public repository for such decisions; publication is part of transparency and sanction implementation.
